findings.evidence: - Send anything, edit the user's files, or reach external systems. You are read-only.
findings.fix: Delete this line. The frontmatter `tools: Read, Glob, Grep` already makes the agent read-only, and the line 14 sentence 'You suggest; the user decides and sends' already covers sending. Use the freed line for a non-obvious communication gotcha.

findings.evidence: - Rewrite so heavily that the user's facts or voice change; flag a factual gap and ask rather than fill it.
findings.fix: Keep only the non-obvious half: 'flag a factual gap and ask rather than fill it.' Cut the generic 'do not over-rewrite' advice, or give a concrete limit, for example 'keep at least the user's opening and closing sentences unless they carry the biggest risk.'

findings.evidence: Review (an outline uses the template with Category = structure)
findings.fix: Give presentation outlines their own short procedure. For example: 'For an outline, check in order: (1) does the decision or ask come in the first slide or minute, (2) does every section answer a question the audience has at that point, (3) is there a fallback if the room rejects the main option. Report each gap as a structure suggestion.' Today the outline branch gets only a category label and no expert sequence.

findings.evidence: ## Gotchas has only two items (deadline softening, Cc'ing a manager)
findings.fix: Add one or two more gotchas from real experience. For example: 'A Slack message that opens with only "hey, got a minute?" leaves the reader anxious and idle: put the ask in the same message.' Or: 'In an architecture review, "we could consider" reads as optional to senior readers: state the recommendation as the recommendation.'

feedback-mastery is preloaded via `skills:` (line 9), so a handoff to it does not resolve: the agent cannot tell whether to deliver structured feedback itself or decline. Replace it with: 'Structured feedback: apply the preloaded feedback-mastery skill (SBI) inside Review or Roleplay; hand off only when the user wants a feedback document written from scratch (`/compose-email` for an email).'

findings.evidence: Route: draft or outline given -> Review ... upcoming conversation, no draft -> Roleplay
findings.fix: Add a rule for the case the router misses, when the user has talking points or a draft and also has an upcoming conversation: 'Draft plus upcoming conversation -> Review first, then offer Roleplay using the revised wording.'

findings.evidence: "Remove hedging that signals real uncertainty just to sound confident" and "Put an inferred motive ... in SBI Behavior" repeat uncertainty-preservation and observable-behavior rules already injected through professional-communication and feedback-mastery.
findings.fix: Consolidate the duplicated uncertainty, SBI and factual-fidelity explanations into a brief instruction to apply the preloaded skills' accuracy and SBI gates. Keep the coach-specific risk prioritization, safety-flag preservation and roleplay rules.

findings.evidence: "ask dropped -> repeat the concern, resistant; resolved -> new concern, confused; over-conceded -> cooperative" has no outcome for a reply that retains the ask but leaves the objection unresolved, such as "I understand, but we still need it Friday."
findings.fix: Add an explicit branch: when the ask is retained but the objection remains unresolved, stay with the same concern and probe the missing constraint, evidence or trade-off; advance to a new concern only after the current one is addressed.

findings.evidence: Add hashtag stacks, "link in bio", or unrelated @mentions or links. ... Write ragebait or exclusionary tribal framing (line 38)
findings.fix: Shorten the generic social-media hygiene items (hashtag stacks, ragebait) to one line each or merge them. Current models already avoid these. Keep the space for the non-obvious items such as the weighted counting, compression falsifying claims and fancy-text cost.

Give lever (b) the same concrete technique that (a) and (c) have. For example: end with one specific question the author genuinely wants answered, tied to the supplied facts, never a generic 'thoughts?'. Then the agent can tell a reply-led draft apart from the engagement bait banned in NEVER.

findings.evidence: numbered posts `1/n ...`, each with its weighted count
findings.fix: Add a Gotcha that the '1/n ' prefix and any thread emoji count toward each post's 280-character weighted limit. Tell the agent to count the post with the prefix included, so a thread post that fits without the prefix does not end up over the limit.

State that the one-liner only replaces scheme-prefixed URLs. A bare domain such as example.com/launch is also auto-linked by X and counts as 23. Tell the agent to add https:// to every link before counting, or extend the regex to catch bare domains, so drafts with short bare links are not undercounted.

findings.evidence: "Open a curiosity loop the post never closes ("you won't believe what happened..." with no payoff): readers feel cheated and stop trusting the account." By source-line count, the familiar Voice and tone guidance, mostly activation-level NEVER list and repeated Output instructions outweigh the more distinctive compression and Unicode gotchas.
findings.fix: Condense familiar tone, engagement-bait and curiosity-gap reminders into a brief activation checklist while retaining their reasons. Replace repetition with a compact worked transformation demonstrating how to change a hook without losing scope, baseline or causal meaning.

findings.evidence: "choose one primary objective: replies, reposts or dwell" and "It decides which variant you RECOMMEND" establish objectives, but the subsequent discussion-versus-standalone guidance covers replies and reach without comparable selection criteria for dwell or sensitive-post clarity.
findings.fix: Add an objective-based comparison before recommending: for dwell, require a concrete observation and a complete lesson or story payoff without withholding information; for clarity, prefer the quiet variant with the least ambiguity or emotional spin. Use these checks to select or revise a candidate rather than relying on its hook/reply/repost label.

findings.evidence: The prescribed `re.sub(r"https?://\S+","x"*23,sys.stdin.read().strip())` and per-code-point sum are labelled "(twitter-text weights)". The regex consumes sentence-final URL punctuation: 256 ASCII letters, a space and `https://example.com.` are counted as 280 rather than 281. The sum also overcounts multi-code-point emoji sequences.
findings.fix: Replace the regex and ordinal-sum counter with a twitter-text-compatible validator that handles URL boundaries, normalization and emoji sequences, such as twitter-text's parseTweet(text).weightedLength. Recount after each revision against the applicable ceiling; retain a conservative margin and label counts approximate when an accurate validator is unavailable.
